work.name: ROAM: Memory-Driven Active Observation for Open-Vocabulary Object Retrieval
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Xiaolong Wang, UC San Diego
highlights: Designed the perception, memory, exploration, and navigation subsystems; proposed a memory-completeness-driven revisit scheduler that plans multi-degree-of-freedom viewpoints and improved object recall from 28.8% to 46.7%.
Built YOLO-World, SAM2, and 3D association pipelines, and introduced anchor-keyframe-relative pose storage to eliminate accumulated SLAM drift, keeping median object-localization error within 12 cm.
Evaluated the system on GOAT-Bench, improving memory-retrieval success from 0.166 to 0.238 and reducing navigation path length to known targets from 55.1 m to 5.8 m, with a 7.2× improvement in SPL.
Deployed the system on a Dexmate Vega wheeled humanoid robot and designed an adaptive recovery strategy that reduced exploration runs invalidated by getting stuck from approximately 33% to 0%.

work.name: HuG: Humanoid Whole-Body Affordance-Aware Grasping with Active Perception
work.summary: Advisor: Prof. Xiaolong Wang, UC San Diego · CoRL 2026
highlights: Proposed the Perceive-Align-Grasp (PAG) embodied-intelligence framework and designed a Bayesian-belief active perception algorithm in the Perceive stage; maintained a probability distribution over a yaw–height viewpoint grid and improved target detection success under severe occlusion from 57.5% to 92.5%.

Bridged perception and downstream whole-body control by aligning active-perception viewpoints online with the input distribution of a CVAE-based grasping policy, and used multidimensional point-cloud quality metrics to determine when to stop observing; stabilized post-detection grasping success at 87.0%.

Integrated Python, PyTorch, ROS2, OpenCV, and point-cloud processing modules; deployed and validated the complete system on a Unitree G1 humanoid robot equipped with a 3-DoF active head and dexterous hands, improving end-to-end success on multi-shelf tasks from 50% to 87.5%.

Trained exclusively on simulation data without real demonstrations and achieved zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, reaching 90% (seen) and 85% (novel) whole-body grasping success rates on the real robot.

work.name: Hikvision Research Institute
highlights: Replaced fixed scoring rules with CLIP cross-modal similarity and reranked image-text results across more than 50,000 product queries, improving image–text ranking accuracy by 4.3% relative.
Processed more than 5 TB of image data and helped build an automated data-quality filtering and checkpoint-based resumable-training pipeline, reducing failed-run recovery time by approximately 60%.

Established structured failure-case tagging and an error-diagnosis workflow, reducing model issue localization from the hour scale to the minute scale and forming a complete diagnosis process across data, algorithms, and experimentation systems.

projects.name: Fine-Tuning Qwen3-4B for Reasoning
highlights: Built a three-stage Prompt Engineering, LoRA SFT, and GRPO fine-tuning pipeline, leading the implementation, and improved validation accuracy from 47% to 66.22% under an approximately $50 H100 compute budget.

Addressed training instability caused by inconsistent prompt formats between the SFT and RL stages by designing a prompt-alignment mechanism and hard-prompt boost; quantitatively attributed gains to Prompt Engineering (+12%), SFT (+6%), and GRPO (+1.78%).

projects.name: Can Vision-Language Models Audit Reward Hacking?
highlights: Designed five reward variants across MuJoCo continuous-control tasks, trained 20 PPO policies, constructed a benchmark, and proposed the hackΔ metric to quantify the severity of reward exploitation.

Analyzed anomalous negative hackΔ values in Hopper and Humanoid, formally distinguishing policy exploitation of reward loopholes from policy non-learning as two failure modes and strengthening the rigor of the VLM audit benchmark.

Strengthened the statistical rigor of RL experiments by analyzing the marginal effects of single random seeds, compute constraints, and high training variance reaching up to a 92% coefficient of variation.

projects.name: Robot State Estimation and SLAM
projects.summary: ECE 276A Sensing and Estimation in Robotics (graduate course)
highlights: Derived the linearized point-to-line ICP residual and vectorized k-NN PCA normal estimation with batched eigendecomposition, roughly two orders of magnitude faster than the loop implementation; with GTSAM pose-graph optimization over approximately 1,000 keyframes, reduced start-to-end trajectory error from approximately 2 m to under 0.1 m on both corridor datasets.

Implemented an EKF on SE(3) with uncertainty parameterized in se(3), deriving landmark and pose Jacobians, and wrote a stereo front-end from scratch (Shi-Tomasi corners, pyramidal Lucas–Kanade tracking, forward-backward and epipolar consistency checks) yielding 6,733 feature tracks over 6,393 frames.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving Car with Vision-Based Traffic Sign Recognition
highlights: Trained an end-to-end CNN behavioral-cloning policy on human-driving demonstrations collected on the vehicle, mapping camera frames directly to steering commands, for trajectory reconstruction.

Built and tuned the team’s ROS2 perception-and-control stack on a VESC-driven 1/10-scale vehicle: HSV lane detection, PID steering control, and a four-state machine for blue-tape intersection handling.

Designed and integrated an OCR traffic-sign recognition module that passed real-time textual decision information to the vehicle-control node, achieving 95% recognition accuracy and 10 Hz closed-loop inference in real-world tests.
